where-the-words-sit.text: A state diagram places the words on the identity's lifecycle.
Registering posts the conviction bond, the freeze bond and the pool. A rotation landed by a hunter pays the premium from the pool.
The poison is the owner's lock, cleared by any witnessed rotation. A freeze lets a hunter take the freeze bond when the pool cannot pay, and a deposit rotation refills it.

The reap is the close: a rotation by the next keys parks the identity, and the registry leaf keeps the hash. A later rotation reopens it. A duplicity proof convicts an active or parked identity and takes the conviction bond.
A consumer trusts an active checkpoint only once it is older than the juvenility window.

the-decision-record.text: Two independent readers met these words before any page defined them, and objected to some of the names themselves.
A table with twelve rows records, for each word, the clause every page uses, the readers' objection, the alternatives weighed, and the outcome.
The outcome for every word is keep and define. A rename would also rename a Lean definition, a simulator transition or a planned command, and that cost is recorded rather than paid here.
Poison is kept over lock, hold and seal. Hunter is kept over relayer, keeper and operator. Juvenility window is kept over maturity, settling and aging window.
The reap is kept as the name of the only close; its older meaning, a hunter consuming a paused checkpoint, is retired. The cage is the MPFS project's own word for a store behind one validator.

Parked and convicted are kept over dormant, closed and tombstoned. The freeze bond and the conviction bond replace the older delay bond, divergence bond and registration bond. The pool and the premium are kept, with the witness pool and the stake pool always qualified.

the-name-of-the-design.text: Issues and the wiki from September 2026 call the design the M1 return: the return, inside the first milestone, from an abandoned enforcement economy to a checkpoint that only projects key state.
Reader-facing pages say the accepted design instead. The home page and the roadmap each explain the old name once, so the older record stays readable.

where-else-the-words-are-fixed.text: The simulator's story file carries a glossary with the same clauses, and the consumer checklist is the shortest page that uses most of them.
